chitchat: Quillon turns a page of the berth book and squares it up against the edge of the desk.
He answers the desk phone, says "it does not lock" twice, and puts it down.
He watches a hull come up the fairway and does not look away until it is past.
Quillon writes a bay number on a card, looks at it, and writes it again more clearly.
description: A narrow man in a marina fleece two sizes too generous for him, standing rather than sitting because the stool is behind him and he has decided against it. He has the look of somebody who has answered the same four questions for six years and has got the answers down to one sentence each.

root.text: "Morning." He squares the berth book. "Buying, hiring, or looking for your own?"

text_by_relation.first:
The man behind the desk straightens up as the door goes.

"Ninian Quillon. This is the desk for hulls." He turns the berth book round to face you. "You buy a boat here or hire one, and I tell you where yours is lying. The dock is east, the chandlery is west, and Anchovies is through the north doors."
text_by_relation.known: "Back again." He is already reaching for the berth book. "Buying, hiring, or finding one?"
text_by_relation.familiar: "There you are." He pushes the berth book aside. "What does she need?"

options.label: I want to buy a boat.
How do I take her out?

buy.text: He taps the desk. "This is what we sell. She comes with a full tank and the first free berth, and I write her into the book as soon as you say."

sell_hydro.text: He opens the berth book at the next clean line.

options.label: How do I take her out?

hire.text: He slides a rate card across. "Any hull on the list, for two hours, with a full tank. One at a time. Tie her up here when you are done and she goes back by herself, or bring me the key sooner. No paint or names on a hire."

hire_hydro.text: He checks the board for a free bay.

options.label: How do I take her out?

return.text: He holds out a hand for the key.

keep.text: He points at the berth board behind him. "Four places to keep her, and you pay for the roof." "East, the Dock Hall: under cover, with the hoist and Marit, and the only berth where a hull comes back fully sound. West, through the chandlery, the Hardstanding: cradles in the open, and the cheapest. North of the Hardstanding, the visitor pontoon and the fuel berth: afloat, alongside." "Stand at a berth and berth reads you the board. berth and her name moves her in, if there is room and she is already in this yard. boats tells you where she is now."

drive.text: He points east without turning. "Go to wherever she is lying and board. That puts you aboard. helm puts you at the wheel, and the controls card comes up the first time." "K is the key, and she will not start with the lever open. From the log, conn start, then conn with a bearing or a bell." "Coming home, stop alongside a berth and disembark. That ties her up. Do it on open water and you are swimming. If she dies out there, tow brings her home, and you settle the bill before she goes out again."

fuel.text: He nods north. "The fuel berth, on the north face of the building, east along the gangway from the visitor pontoon. It is the only marine pump on the Basin." "Bring her alongside the pylons, stop, and fuel. You pay by the unit, so a bigger tank costs more to fill."

work.text: "Marit Colvane, in the Dock Hall, east. She is there from nine until six." "Stand in the hall with her there and refit, and Marit puts the hull back to sound wherever your boat is lying in this yard. Servicing, paint and a name need the boat under the roof: berth her in the hall, or bring her into the covered slot and stop. Then refit service, refit paint or refit name." "Away from the hall you patch her yourself. Marit sells hull patches. A patch gets her to about half on the water and most of the way on a cradle."

eat.text: "Anchovies, through the north doors." He points without turning. "Twelve tables over the water, Italian, and dear. Ottavia opens at six in the evening and serves until midnight."

bye.text: "Right." He is back at the berth book before the door has closed.

clothing_layers: a marina fleece with the burgee on the chest, zipped to the throat
a shirt collar turned out over it, which he is aware of
trousers that have been in salt water and recovered

name: Ninian Quillon
